newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: S.E. Asia currencies cool off temporarily.
newsitem.headline: S.E. Asia currencies cool off temporarily.

text.p: Southeast Asia's currency turmoil cooled on Wednesday as the market held off major activity ahead of a rescue package for Thailand's battered economy.
But dealers said they were still looking to buy the U.S. dollar whenever it weakened.

Optimism about Thailand's plans to seek assistance from the International Monetary Fund (IMF) in rehabilitating its economy continued to underpin the baht and lent support to the region's other currencies as well.

But dealers said the baht's gains were likely to be limited to about 31 to the dollar for the time being as market operators would play it safe on the baht ahead of the government's economic rescue package, expected by August 5.
The baht was quoted at 31.60/80 to the dollar onshore at 0400 GMT against 31.50-31.80 late on Tuesday. It was at 31.15/35 offshore.
Bangkok dealers said the baht was supported earlier by some repatriation of funds by exporters.
In Malaysia, Prime Minister Mahathir Mohahamad's continued tirade against currency speculation spurred further caution as he extended his criticism to local operators.

Kuala Lumpur newspapers quoted Mahathir as saying Malaysians became involved in the recent attacks on the ringgit by making the currency available to speculators and may also have been seeking profit themselves.
"The market feels that if he continues to talk this way, there may be some action down the line. So people are wary," said an analyst with a research firm in Singapore.
The chief regional currency dealer at a European bank in Singapore said Mahathir's remarks were prompting Kuala Lumpur corporates and exporters to sell the dollar on any rallies.
But he said the dollar was also being supported near the 2.6150 ringgit level by local corporate and U.S. fund buying interest.
The ringgit was at 2.6175/205 to the dollar at 0400 GMT.
The Singapore dollar was also on firmer footing, helped by the U.S. dollar's failure to rise above S$1.4650 overnight and its easier tone against the mark.
But dealers said the Singapore dollar's rise would be blocked around 1.4560 to the U.S. dollar for now.

The Indonesian rupiah remained ensconced above the 2,600 level to the dollar but dealers said local operators continued to buy dollars following central bank statements that a normal level for the rupiah was between 2,555 and 2,610.
A U.S. bank dealer in Jakarta said the rupiah looked set to trade between 2,560 and 2,580 throughout the day.
Spot rupiah was quoted at 2,563/72 at 0400 GMT, compared with an opening of 2,565/75.
Indonesia's central bank was reported to have sold $1 billion in the forward market to stabilise the rupiah during last week's speculative attack.

The Jakarta Post newspaper quoted central bank governor Sudradjad Djiwandono as saying the amount was less than that spent by Thailand and the Philippines to defend their currencies because the bank had acted pre-emptively by widening its dollar-rupiah band.
The Philippine central bank sold dollars at the higher level of 29 pesos on Wednesday amid persistent dollar demand from commercial clients.
Traders said the demand was unlikely to subside and the peso would fall sharply if the central bank did not step in.

The Taiwan dollar opened sharply lower and was expected to trade in a volatile range of T$28.20-50 after the central bank allowed it to fall through the T$28 level for the first time since 1989 on Tuesday.
